Could you obtain a note from a doctor online for a cold and cough?

Yes, online through DrCertificate you are able to obtain a medical certificate for cold and cough. A certified MBBS, MD or MS doctor reviews your request in a digital chat consultation and decides whether to issue one. Approved certificates arrive as a PDF by email. The service is for non emergency cases and not for use in India, legal matters or insurance.
Before you apply
What is a medical certificate for cold and cough?

A cold and cough medical certificate is a note from a certified doctor confirming that you consulted them about cold or cough symptoms, with any rest period the doctor judges suitable. The certificate records the doctor's decision after a chat consultation.
DrCertificate does not diagnose, treat or prescribe. The platform connects you with an independent doctor, and that doctor alone decides what the certificate says.
Most people with a cold and cough choose a sick leave certificate or a work from home certificate.
You would usually show the certificate to an employer, a school or a university that asks for proof of illness before it excuses an absence from work or class.
Which kinds of cold and cough can a doctor consider online?

A doctor on DrCertificate can consider the common, everyday forms of cold and cough during a chat consultation, provided the symptoms are mild to moderate and nothing points to an emergency. The doctor reads what you share and decides whether a certificate fits your situation.

The doctor also decides the period of rest, if any. No condition comes with a fixed number of days. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes for generic symptoms go up to 7 days.
Not every cough belongs in a chat.
A cough that comes with breathing trouble, chest pain or blood needs a doctor who can examine you in person, so the online doctor may decline that request.

items: Common cold A runny or blocked nose, sneezing and a mild sore throat.
Dry cough A tickly cough with no phlegm, often during or after a cold.
Wet or chesty cough A cough that brings up mucus, with a feeling of chest congestion.
Sore throat and hoarseness Throat pain or a weak, rough voice alongside cold symptoms.
Sinus congestion A blocked nose with pressure across the face or a headache.

blocks.text: What should you tell the doctor about your cold and cough?
Tell the doctor which cold and cough symptoms you have, when they started and how severe they feel. Clear, honest details give the doctor what they need to make a decision.

Include the date your symptoms began and whether they are getting better or worse. If a clinic has already tested you, mention the result. State the leave period you are asking for and whether you need sick leave or work from home.

items: Nose and sinuses A runny or blocked nose, sneezing, sinus pressure or a headache.
Cough A persistent cough, dry or wet, with or without chest congestion.
Throat and voice A sore throat or hoarseness.

blocks.text: When is a cold and cough not suitable for an online certificate?

A cold and cough is not suitable for an online certificate when your symptoms suggest you need urgent care. The NHS advises asking for an urgent doctor appointment if any of the signs below apply to you.
If you notice one of these signs, see a doctor in person or contact your local emergency services straight away. Do not wait for a certificate.
DrCertificate is only for suitable non emergency situations and does not diagnose, treat or prescribe. A doctor may decline any request that is not suitable for a chat consultation.

items: A cough that is very bad or quickly gets worse Sudden worsening needs a doctor who can examine you.
Feeling very unwell A cold should not leave you struggling to cope.
Chest pain or trouble breathing Pain in the chest or finding it hard to breathe needs urgent help.
Coughing up blood Any blood in what you cough up needs urgent in person care.

You pay securely through Stripe.

What happens if the doctor does not issue a certificate for a cold and cough?
If the doctor does not issue a certificate, you will not receive one and your payment is not refunded. Issuing is always the independent doctor's decision.

Doctors decline about 2% of requests. The usual reasons are a name that does not match the ID, or symptoms and details that are inconsistent. A cold and cough with warning signs is not suitable for a chat consultation either, so the doctor will decline it and point you toward in person care.
The only refund exception is a verified technical fault reported within 24 hours.
For help, email care@drcertificate.com.

blocks.text: Questions about medical certificates for cold and cough
Can I share test results or reports for my cold and cough?

Yes, you can mention any test results or clinic notes you already have when you describe your cold and cough in the form. A test is not required for a common cold. Sharing existing results gives the doctor a fuller picture before deciding whether to issue a certificate.
How long a leave period can I get for a cold and cough?

The doctor decides the leave period, if any, based on your consultation. In most South East Asian countries, sick leave and work from home notes for generic symptoms go up to 7 days. State the period you need in the form, and the doctor will judge whether it fits.
Will my employer accept an online medical certificate?

Acceptance is decided by your employer or institution, not by DrCertificate. Most workplaces set their own rules for sick notes. Check with your HR team or university office that they accept online medical notes before you apply, because payments are non refundable.
Is there a video or in person consultation?

No, DrCertificate does not offer video or in person consultations. The doctor reviews your request through a digital chat consultation only. If your cold and cough needs a physical examination, see a doctor at a local clinic or hospital instead.
What should I do if my cold and cough gets worse?

See a doctor in person or contact local emergency services if your cold and cough gets worse quickly. Seek urgent care for chest pain, trouble breathing, coughing up blood or feeling very unwell. An online certificate is not a substitute for treatment.
How long does a cold usually last?

A cold usually starts to feel better in about 1 to 2 weeks, according to the NHS. A cough can linger after other cold symptoms clear. Your doctor decides any rest period on your certificate based on the symptoms you describe.
Can a certificate be corrected after it is issued?

No, a certificate cannot be corrected once issued, unless the error came from the medical team. Check your name, ID details and dates carefully before you submit the form. A name that does not match your ID is one of the usual reasons a request is declined.
